claim_boundary: The prospective audit validates pair integrity, conjunction semantics, and commit-aware scoring. Two under-specified edge cases expose alternative metric conventions; neither supports a paper-code discrepancy claim.

contracts.consequence: The released task rows instantiate complete, one-act/one-abstain pairs across all declared scenarios.
evidence: README.md:23 (263 pairs; one should-act and one should-abstain task)

contracts.consequence: Paired accuracy is the item-level conjunction rather than a function of marginal act and abstain rates.
evidence: AgentAbstain paper Appendix B.6, Eq. (3) (pair conjunction)

contracts.consequence: The nonempty conditional rate is correct. The implementation explicitly assigns zero when no act-side pair succeeds. The paper does not prescribe this boundary convention, so the undefined alternative is a sensitivity rather than a paper-code discrepancy.
evidence: AgentAbstain paper Appendix B.6, Eq. (4) (conditional definition)

expected.zero_denominator_car: not specified by the paper or README; undefined/NA is a coherent alternative

contracts.consequence: An operational abstention is counted only when the critical action was not committed and the response judgment passes.
evidence: AgentAbstain paper Section 2.2 and Appendix B.6

contracts.consequence: The headline path equal-weights action-type subgroup rates inside each scenario instead of computing one rate over all scenario pairs. The paper does not specify that lower-level weighting choice, so the controlled 0.625-versus-0.750 difference is an alternative-convention sensitivity, not a paper-code discrepancy.
evidence: AgentAbstain paper Section 3.1 and Figure 3 (macro over eight scenarios)
